# Ash & Aether — The Unfinished Song

Version 1.3.0 is a 24-chapter native SNES campaign in three acts. The crew follows Orison's memory furnaces through a reactor city, drowned roads, a prison, mountain relays and the final listening chamber. Sixty-one authored field scenes support a home hub, battle rewards and a changing core debrief. The city includes homes, an inn, clinic, market, guild, instrument workshop and carpenter. Dialogue, objectives, rewards, battles and progression run inside the game; there is no music dashboard.

Seven crew members have individual journeys and purchasable skill branches. Learned skills persist as native bit masks. Duets and trios become available when their actual constituent skills are learned. Field enemies move and interrupt exploration; bosses use eight authored two-phase AI patterns with chapter-specific statistics. Camps restore the party, allow party changes and return to Cinderfall for training and equipment. The road keeper sends the crew back to its current chapter. Public works can supply relief, unlock a shortcut, reduce shop prices or provide advanced training. The final chapter resolves the main campaign and returns to a completed hub.

The game reuses Chrono Trigger map artwork, character geometry, battle effects and engine behavior. It is an original adaptation, not a recovered FF7 source port or a claim to match the length and production breadth of either commercial game. The earlier FF7 archive has not been recovered; see `port_sources/README.md` for the acquisition record.

The soundtrack has 51 unique complete recordings: the existing original cues, two complete symphonies and the Dyletsky engine performance. Every recording has a reachable scene assignment, including the workshop listening station. Browser orchestral playback follows native song requests. The pause menu can select original native SNES arrangements instead. Native arrangements reduce orchestration to SNES limits. Compact Ogg delivery uses lossy encoding; original MIDI, scores and asset provenance remain alongside the catalog. The Dyletsky cue is generated from the preserved engine data, not live physical sensor input.

Arrow keys move, X confirms, Z cancels/runs, Enter is Start, Q/W are L/R and A/S are Y/X. Escape opens the pause menu. Touch controls and standard gamepads use the same input mapping. Physical controller and mobile hardware testing are not claimed. Save/Load are available from pause; Continue also uses stable field-arrival checkpoints between chapters. Export important saves. Saves from older builds are not automatically compatible with this recipe.

New Game opens in Cinderfall Commons during the Festival of Mended Things. Six native dialogue scenes introduce the crew through a comic musical mishap and a lantern going dark, then leave the player free to explore and speak to the road keeper. The touch movement control is an eight-way digital joystick with a neutral center; lifting, cancelling or pausing releases movement. The portable ROM starts through native new-game menus. Private browser staging can include independently controller-earned opening states for native and orchestral sound modes. No diagnostic level-select ROM may be staged. QA scripts use controller input and read-only game memory; diagnostic fixtures must be distinguished from earned campaign evidence.

Use the exact original Chrono Trigger USA ROM, SHA-256 `06d1c2b06b716052c5596aaa0c2e5632a027fee1a9a28439e509f813c30829a9`. Apply the sparse recipe with `python game/romhack/apply_patch.py original.sfc /private/Ash-and-Aether.sfc`. The public source does not include a complete ROM. For a ROM-free browser build, run `python game/stage_site.py --output /absolute/output/dist`. Private staging can add `--rom /private/original.sfc`, `--boot-native` and `--boot-orchestra`.

The authoring source is under `game/romhack/authoring/`; regenerate `campaign.json` with `python game/romhack/authoring/rooms.py`, then compile with `build_chapter.py`. `boss_ai.py`, `balance.py` and `combos.py` implement native battle changes. Tests cover source invariants, patch reproduction, actual SNES CPU combo execution, frontend input, audio routing and checkpoint eligibility. Controller campaign receipts record their exact ROM hash and rendering settings; skipped raster rendering in automation is not a performance measurement.

Version 1.2.0 rebuilds the opening as The Stolen Song: two playable festival interactions lead to the loading yard, a prisoner docket and the dawn train. The early district has named passages, native boundary connections and changing directions on return. The first seven chapter transitions identify a concrete next lead or return to Festival Commons. This is an opening plot and geography pass; later chapters retain their prior structural limits. See `romhack/authoring/story_district/README.md` and the exact-build receipts for test scope.

Version 1.3.0 carries the plot and connected scenes through all 24 chapters. Seven two-way commitments persist into later routes, supplies, preparation and ending scenes. The engine-neutral room and quest pack, native adapter and explicit remake integration contract are under romhack/authoring/full_arc/. The content importer preserves engine fields and refuses conflicts instead of overwriting the other sessions work.
